identity.realm: Seventh gate held, and the eighth is the liver: the last ordinary vessel and the largest, the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened. The fire half of his crossing puts a heavier mineral load through a blood that is already filtering stone, so his ceiling is structural rather than a matter of effort. He has stood at the approach to it enough times to have worn a groove in himself, and calls it a decision.

appearance.presentation: A face built to be looked at briefly, at a distance, and in bad light. Everything about it works and nothing about it rests, and the whole impression is of a man who is already on his way somewhere else.
appearance.age: Unstated. The guild roster carries a birth year and he has never confirmed it. An emberhollow's lungs date a body more honestly than a face does, so strangers read him younger and everyone who has actually worked him reads him older, and neither reading has ever been wrong by more than a decade.
appearance.build: Compact and heavy, short-waisted, with the shoulders and forearms of somebody who has swung a pick since he was tall enough to hold it, and a chest that flares visibly on the exhale and takes a moment to come back down.
appearance.complexion: Grey-flecked at the throat and along the collarbone, hot to the touch through the cloth, with a fine rime of ash sitting on him that does not fall off when he moves.
appearance.hair: Cut short and unevenly, gone white in a hard band at the temples, singed along one side at a length the other side has never had.
appearance.eyes: Bloodshot, quick, and by a considerable margin the warmest thing left in him.
appearance.palette: Charcoal, oxide red, and one cold blue for the guild. The blue is the house colour of a standing order, and he wears it because standing orders wear the house colour.
appearance.attire: High-collared ash-cloth with the sleeves doubled and burned through at both cuffs, a leather apron carrying a stone-dust bloom, split-toed boots worn down at the outer edge. No jewellery, on the guild rule that anything metal worn by a furnace worker is stored somewhere the Ironpact can reach it.
appearance.marks: A pale grey bloom worked into his collar and the top of the apron where sweat has been left to dry against stone dust. Three separate people have read it as a dye marker for his contract tier, and he has never corrected any of them.
appearance.bearing: Upright and quick, with a hitch between movements now that he is dosing, and a habit of turning his head to listen that outruns whatever the sound actually was.

canon.role_in_story: A standing order is priced in a body that does not have to be relieved, and the body that does not have to be relieved is the one already burning out. He is the best contractor on the belt because his rate of cultivation is the fastest in any record, and that rate buys exactly one useful thing, which is a breakthrough every few years in a body whose lungs scar on a fixed clock whether it breaks through or not. He has solved the only problem a fast-burning body actually has, which is being legible before it finishes: he doses on an interval instead of on a symptom, so his decline is the most evenly documented case in the region and the one institution holding the complete figure is the guild he works for. What nobody builds a horizon around is the shape of the thing. They build a week.
canon.first_appearance: First seen walking out of a working face two hours after a shift change he was not rostered for, and the reason given, twice and in the same words, by two people who had no way of agreeing with each other, was that he was not waiting for the remedy.
canon.lore: An emberhollow is the fire body crossed with the ash body, and it is the fastest cultivator in the setting by a margin nobody has explained. The rate comes from a frame that runs the ash parent's mineral sieve hot enough to process faster than the sieve was built to run, which means it also scars faster, and the organ that fails under that burden is the liver — the eighth gate, the last ordinary vessel and the largest, the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened. Their ceiling is inherited from the ash parent and made worse by the fire parent. They are the best and the shortest-lived cultivators in any record, and that is a single fact and not two. The mind path is closed outright, so the insight that would let a body plan its own decline at the only horizon that matters is unavailable to it, which is why the settled practice among them is a written interval rather than a judgement. Everything around that biology conspires to make the interval unnecessary and impossible. The tier's only dependable remedy is rationed by a rule whose first priority is grazers, because the herds are larger than the households and the commons has no defender except the people who can do without it, which is nobody — and that rule was written for an emergency, in which a body that cannot reach the queue dies before it is missed. An emberhollow needs the same remedy on a schedule, which is the one use the rule was never written for. The first knowledge here that is bought rather than inherited is a method for timing a breakthrough to a tide, and it is worth nothing outside its own tier, so the fastest cultivator in the setting depends on a scheduling technology built for bodies that can wait. And the working stone remembers: a grey lichen colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, the trace never washes off, and the densest lichen anywhere on the plains is underground where this body works. The only complete record of a fast-burning cultivator's life is a growth pattern on a rock face, and it is legible from above.
history: Was born on the belt rather than off it, which the crossing explains and the family did not: nobody chose a fire body and an ash body to meet on a shared border, and that is what a shared border produces.

Learned the dosing interval from a written sheet that has been in the family for three generations and has never once been revised, because revising it would require the mind path his crossing closed, and nobody in the family has ever had the standing to say so out loud.

Was entered on the Ironpact's standing order at nineteen, which is earlier than the charter recommends and earlier than the guild's own medical clause allows, and was entered because he was already refusing to stop on a shift and the guild priced the refusal as a skill.

Discovered that the lichen under his working faces thickened on a schedule he could read from above, and began keeping his interval in the same units — a band of pale stone, a shift, a dose. Three guild clerks have since copied the practice and none of them has understood what they are reading.
Stood at the approach to the eighth gate once, came back down, and has since described it to exactly one person as a decision rather than a failure. He does not know whether it was one.

Began refusing relief at the face, on the argument that a man who is not relieved is a man whose decline is not yet in anybody's ledger, and discovered within a season that the ledger had recorded him anyway, in the guild's roster, in a column he cannot read and cannot reach.

personality.summary: Methodical to a degree that reads as cold and is not. He has made the worst arithmetic fact about his own body the most legible fact about himself, and he takes more pride in the interval sheet than in any gate he has ever passed.
traits: keeps a written interval and has never once missed it, including the two occasions on which missing it would have been indistinguishable from succeeding
states his own decline as a date rather than a condition, in conversation, without being asked and without any visible weight
reads a works face faster than anyone on the belt and has never once been asked to read anything else
is loyal to the guild in the specific sense that he believes a roster is a promise, and would leave a guild that broke one
cannot plan past a horizon and has stopped pretending the limitation is a choice
refuses any technique, elixir or contract term that would delay his decline without stating his reason, and has been described by three separate guild clerks as being difficult about scheduling
mannerisms: counts aloud under his breath on long carries, in sevens, and loses count when he reaches the eighth and starts again
drinks standing, always facing the working face, and will not sit down on a shift
touches the stone at the top of a ladder before he sets weight on it
answers a question about his future with the length of a shift
wipes the stone dust off his collar and then puts his hand flat on the bloom afterwards, which he has never been asked to explain
motivations: wants the interval sheet to outlast him as a working document rather than a memorial
wants one decision, on the record, that the eighth gate is a wall and not a shortfall, because the guild has been pricing him as though it were the second
wants his decline recorded somewhere a person would have to read
wants, once, to be asked what he thinks he is for, and has arranged his whole working life so that this has never come up
flaws: cannot read his own body inward — the mind path is closed and the insight that would let him judge the interval is in the crossing, so the sheet is the only opinion he has and it is four generations old
has made being legible into a substitute for being asked, and cannot tell the difference between the two
withholds the one piece of information every person he contracts with actually needs, which is the interval, because handing it over turns him from a contractor into an obituary
refuses relief in a way that costs him nothing and costs whoever is standing next to him the whole of the risk, and he has never been able to make that arithmetic come out in his favour
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried, and entirely numerical where a number exists. Speaks in shifts, loads and intervals rather than in feelings about them, and answers a question he does not like with a figure. Breaks off mid-sentence when he coughs and resumes at the same word without any apology for the interval, which is the only unreliable thing about how he talks.
taboos: will not take an elixir or a contract term that would slow the decline without telling the counterparty plainly what it costs
will not let anyone else read the interval sheet, and has moved it twice rather than explain why
will not be described as brave, and has ended more than one conversation by leaving a room
will not discuss the eighth gate except as a decision, and has never once described it as one in front of the same person twice
will not be relieved on a face, and has never accepted relief without also accepting that the refusal is written down

relationships.note: The tier's only dependable remedy, with a dosing rule that puts grazers first because the herds are larger than the households. That rule was written for an emergency, in which a body that cannot reach the queue dies before it is missed. He needs the same remedy on a schedule, which is the one use the rule was never written for, so the fastest-burning cultivator in the region is permanently served last by the only thing that would slow him.

A grey lichen that colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, and the trace never washes off. The densest lichen anywhere on the plains is under the faces he has worked, in bands that match his interval sheet. The only complete record of his body's whole life is a growth pattern on a rock face and it is legible from above, which is a court record nobody can edit and the only one of him he did not have to write.

A guild-house that sells capacity: members are the muscle it rents out to whoever is paying, and it keeps a roster of names whose labour is worth more than any individual contract. He has been on the standing order since he was nineteen. The roster is simultaneously the best contract list on the belt and the most accurate mortality record on the plains, and neither fact was ever a decision anybody took.

A culture that keeps no growing store of the long-lived and instead holds the year's dead together as a single declared group, because a body of fifty years thinned at exactly the rate it could not stop. He is the crossing that would have solved that famine if the mineral load had not sealed the liver first, and he is the fastest producer of exactly the entry the group exists to declare.

Tier six, the last ordinary vessel to open, at rung eight, the largest of the twelve and the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened. Damaged, a body can still cultivate and simply stops being able to. He stands at the approach to it in a body that is already filtering stone faster than the sieve was built to run, and has described the single attempt he made as a decision.

A breakthrough prepared rather than attempted: a dose timed to the tide that will carry it, on a stone bed that holds qi. It is the first knowledge here that is bought rather than inherited, and it is worth nothing outside its own tier because a tide cannot be read on any frame below the peaks. The fastest cultivator in the setting therefore depends entirely on a scheduling technology built for bodies that can wait, and he has never once been the kind of body it was written for.

reference_stats.summary: The strongest body-cultivator in the setting and the shortest-lived one with a gate above the fourth. An ember-blood frame running an ash sieve hot enough to be the fastest thing on the belt and hot enough to be eating itself, and the distance between those two statements is a clock rather than a dispute.
strengths: draws and cultivates qi faster than anything else on record, by a margin measured in how much further a crew gets in a week
works a hot face for a full shift and does not need relieving, which makes him the only contractor the guild can put on continuous work
reads worked stone and load the way a clerk reads a board, and has never been asked to read anything that is not stone
breaks through more often in a short life than most cultivators manage in a long one, and each one arrives faster than the method that prepared it was built to deliver
is already legible — decline measured, dated and on file — so nothing about his condition is ever a surprise to anyone but himself
weaknesses: lungs that scar on a fixed schedule nothing in the record slows, so his usable span is a few decades and every gain is bought at the wrong exchange rate
a hard ceiling at the liver, inherited from the ash parent and made worse by the fire half, which no amount of effort reaches
no mind path and poor insight, so he cannot judge his own condition inward and depends on a written sheet four generations old
leaner and slower to mend than a body that is not burning through its own reserve, which means a serious wound arrives before a fight does
cannot slow himself down, and every delay he causes a crew has cost the crew rather than him
reference_stats.combat_read: He fights close, with the tools he works with, because his rate lives in his own reserve and not in anything he can hold. A drawn-out exchange is a losing exchange: the faster he goes the more of himself he spends and there is no store to spend out of. Two hard minutes is his whole event and all of it is front-loaded. Anything that makes him stop and re-approach has already won most of it. He cannot be warned about his own decline, and he is the only opponent in the setting who arrives knowing exactly how long he has.
notes: Never write him as reckless. The interval is a discipline with a written record behind it, and the apparent carelessness is the residue of a body that cannot afford caution.
His best quality and his worst are the same fact — the fastest cultivation rate in the record — and any scene that resolves one has to account for the other in the same breath.
The closed mind path is mechanical, not moody. He does not brood; he has no instrument to brood with, and has said so.

art.palette_notes: Charcoal and ash-grey base, oxide red in the heat sources and the guild's cold blue in the house trim. He is the warmest object in every frame and the background behind him is always cooler than he is, which is the visual argument the whole character rests on. Stone dust reads as a pale bloom on cloth. Hard directional key from the working light, one bounce off the floor, and no soft light anywhere on him — the scarring does not catch diffuse light and should not be drawn as though it does.

identity.realm: Fifth gate, and the sixth was not a wall he failed — it was a wall he has nowhere to put. The qi network is a fast single loop with no storage at all, so every gate this body opens is a gate it cannot hold. Its breakthroughs are early and terminal by construction, and the rate it absorbs at is the fastest on the ash, and none of that is an achievement: it is a loop that passes everything through.

appearance.presentation: Long-legged, low-headed and plated, with a second stomach that audibly works and a tail used as a counterbalance rather than a hand. It reads at distance as a shape crossing ash, and it does not read at all if it decides not to, which it can.
appearance.age: Read off the second stomach's ferment line and the wear on the rear teeth, which is how every pack reads it and the only reckoning of age anyone has ever applied to one. It is past the point where a litter-mate would still be recognisable by scent and has been for some time.
appearance.build: All of the mass in the forelimbs. The hindquarters are narrow and the gait is built to shed rather than to hold, because a four-legged frame has no hindquarter girth with which to close the girdling vessel — which is the whole of why the extraordinary network never finished assembling in this body.
appearance.complexion: Short ash-grey fur over a plated skull, with the heat-shedding skin at the flanks bare and faintly pink, and a permanent dusting of spoil on the hind legs that no amount of grooming removes because the ground it walks is the dust.
appearance.hair: Coarse guard hairs along the spine that lift when it is reading a gradient, so the ridge of its back is a display it cannot switch off.
appearance.eyes: Amber, deep-set under the plate's overhang, and wider than any head at that size should manage. They are the only part of it that is not built for heat.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, bleached bone, and one band of dull oxide where guild paint has come off a spoil crate and onto its ribs. Three colours and a foreign mark.
appearance.attire: Nothing worn. The band of transferred paint across the ribs, halfway worn off, is the closest thing this animal has ever had to a uniform and it was not issued to it.
appearance.marks: A notched left ear with four old cuts in the lobe, a healed split at the right jaw, and the paint band. Nothing about any of it was done for its benefit.
appearance.bearing: Weight always on the forelimbs and never on the hindquarters, head low, tail level, and a stance that reads as about to leave rather than about to arrive. It has never once been photographed facing the camera and there are four photographs of it.

canon.role_in_story: A scavenger is born where the dead are the most reliable food, and a pack is a kinship by scent that dissolves when the scent changes — which is why packs are not families and why a population built entirely out of what other people leave behind is also a population with no line of descent to be inherited along. This one holds the leeward gradient immediately below the one settlement on the tier whose whole population is visitors, and it has held the same relay position since the rest of the pack dissolved, so the only thing it exists to be has been gone for years and everything it still reports arrives at nobody. Its map is the one public account on the plains — a tally of spoil moved by every crew, kept where the crews can read it — and the tally is a weight rather than a distance, which makes it simultaneously the only map on the tier and the only one no two readers have ever agreed about. Nothing it reports can be cited, because scent is not testimony and a relay is not a witness, and a gradient cannot be located to open a case. That is the whole reason a population can be cleared off a slope without a hearing, and it is why the one creature on the plains that never lies to anybody has never once been asked a question.
canon.first_appearance: First noticed as a shape moving along the leeward line on precisely the days the public spoil tally changed, four hundred paces below the stair, and never once inside the light. It took four separate observers and a comparison of the tally's arithmetic against the animal's line before anyone agreed it was not a loose dog.
canon.lore: An ashjackal is an obligate scavenger: long-legged and low-headed, with a plated skull that dissipates heat, a second stomach for fermentation, and a tail that is a counterbalance rather than a manipulator. All of the mass is in the forelimbs. Olfaction is a map — the body reads a qi gradient through ash at a distance no sight-based predator can match, and the pack relay carries that reading to every other member within seconds. It has no spoken vocabulary and no vocalisation that carries meaning; the entire channel is scent, gland and posture, and a member's position in the relay is a fixed place in a fixed order, not a name. A pack is a kinship by scent and dissolves when the scent changes, which is the mechanism by which a scavenger population is shaped by whatever is left rather than by anything it did. The mind path is closed because a heat-exchange brainplate leaves no cortical folding for introspection to work on, and the body path is closed because qi cannot be stored in a frame built to shed heat; the extraordinary network is a fast single loop with nothing to hold anything, so the breakthroughs come early and are terminal. Qi is the only open path and it is fast — residual qi out of ash and carcass at a rate nothing else matches — because a body that eats what qi leaves behind is a body with an unusually direct relationship to the leftovers of cultivation. What it cannot do is take a healthy adult of anything: it eats the aftermath and is out of a live fight in under a minute. It follows carrion populations and does not precede them, and it holds the gradient on the leeward side of anything that kills in quantity. It has no homeland of that kind; it has a gradient. And because no march order on the plains can be enforced by measurement — every claim there is settled by a marker left standing, and nothing survives a gradient that feeds on it — the scavenger is the population that turns standing into a question rather than a formality.
history: Was born in a litter on the spoil, which is the only food supply on the tier that does not run out, because the ground is walked out once and then stands there for decades with everything that made it still inside it.

Took a relay position at the back of a working pack, where the position carried no rank and no name — a gradient is shared by marking and re-reading rather than by being announced, so the ninth place is a place and not a description.
Lost the pack without a death. A pack dissolves when the scent changes, and this one went through it and came out the other side holding a position that no longer had a receiver at the other end.

Began working the public spoil tally instead of the relay, because a tally of weight moved by every crew is where a scavenger's range comes from: crews break where they break and they leave something where they break.

Was cleared off a slope with nobody able to say who ordered it, which took no hearing because a gradient cannot be located well enough to open one, and returned to the same line below the stair within the season.

personality.summary: Not a personality in any sense a person would recognise. What the record has instead is a set of consistent position-readings kept up across years with no audience present, which is the closest a body with no introspection and no vocabulary can get to being reliable.

follows the tally, which is the only published account of where anything has been broken
reads the leeward line, which is the only gradient on the tier that keeps producing
cannot want any of these and relays all three without distinction, which is what has kept it alive this long

has no way to know whether a position is still occupied at the far end, and has kept one anyway for longer than the pack existed
cannot distinguish a gradient belonging to another pack from one belonging to a person, and treats both as the same kind of event
arrives second and has never tested whether it could be first, because first would require being on a face while something is still alive on it
personality.voice: None, and this is the honest word rather than a stylistic one. There is no vocalisation that carries meaning, no learned sound, and nothing that has ever been recorded as an answer. What it produces is gland and posture read by the whole body at once: ear carriage, jaw set, head height, tail level, and the second stomach working. Its reports travel as scent and as angle and are true at the moment they arrive. Four observers have written down that it appeared to answer a question, and all four were describing an animal orienting toward a voice, which is what any animal does.
taboos: will not advance on anything that is still moving with intent, and has turned away from a live fight four separate times in one season
will not enter a lit working area while a crew is still in it
will not take from anything carrion that has not been open for longer than its own certainty
cannot be made to indicate a thing it has not read, and cannot be asked to repeat a reading, because repeating it is not a thing a relay can do

relationships.note: The guild that moves the spoil heap off the seam floor cannot employ what it cannot catch, so the packs are tolerated inside its charter rather than members of it. That arrangement is the reason the waste guild's tally is public where the extraction guild's is not, and the reason a scavenger has a documented range and no documented standing.

A public count of spoil moved by every crew, kept where the crews can read it, and the only accounting the mortal tier can support — because it is a weight and not a distance, and on a frame with no spatial law no two measurements of a length have ever agreed. A scavenger's whole range is a function of where crews break and where they leave something, so this count is the pack's map and the pack's reason to stay out of the guilds' way.

The plains' one large migratory herd returns on a cycle nobody on the ground has predicted, which makes it the tier's only moving calendar. The pack's timing is borrowed wholesale from an animal it does not hunt and cannot follow without eating it, so the one schedule available to it is one it is not permitted to act on.

Strata under the plains carry tool marks that imply a hand, on a frame that seats three law groups and none of them moves distance, so no hand could have worked them. The only population that reaches the bottom of an unmoved spoil heap without moving anything is the one that cannot carry anything at all, and the heap has stood on the ore that is gone for four decades.

Carrionfolk find what is left and ashjackal arrive after them. The order is not negotiable and neither party chose it: one metabolises qi out of the dead and cannot store any, the other eats the remainder, and the second population to arrive is the second because it is the one that waits for the first to have finished.

No march order on the plains can be enforced by measurement, so every claim is settled by a marker left standing, and a scavenger is the population that makes standing a question rather than a formality: nothing survives a gradient that feeds on it, so possession here is proven by a marker and not by where it is, and a marker placed on this slope does not last a season.

reference_stats.summary: The fastest body on the ash and the only one with no way to keep what it takes. Olfaction is a map; the qi network is a fast single loop with no storage at all; the breakthroughs are early and terminal; and in a live fight the entire event is over before either side has properly started it.
strengths: reads a qi gradient through ash at a distance no sight-based predator can match, and relays it to others in seconds
absorbs residual qi out of ash and carcass at a rate nothing else matches, which is the only open path this body has
arrives wherever a thing has already been finished, and can therefore be on ground nobody has left yet
requires no pack to function, and has now demonstrated that for years without any measurable loss
cannot be warned, suppressed or frightened by anything that works through a meridian, because there is no folding for one to work on
leaves nothing to find afterwards, which is why it has never once been the subject of a recovery
weaknesses: cannot take a healthy adult of anything, and is out of a live fight in under a minute by construction
has no store of any kind, so everything it draws passes straight through it and none of it is retained a second longer
cannot be precisely located, which means it cannot be summoned, sworn, owed anything, or protected by any proceeding that requires a location
arrives second by species, so it is structurally dependent on a population it cannot become
has no mind path and therefore no way to reason about what it reads — only the read, at the speed it arrives
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not put it in a fight. It is removed from one in under a minute and the removal is not a defeat — it is simply the end of its participation. It does not guard, does not charge, and does not hold ground; it takes the aftermath, which means a battle fought where the ash is already deep is a battle it will walk into about four minutes after the last person in it has stopped moving. Its qi is borrowed and transient and moves too fast to be aimed at anything, so treating it as a cultivator in a fight is a category error twice over. The only contest this body is actually in is the one it is always winning, which is arriving first.
notes: Never write it speaking, answering, or being understood. Four observers have written down an answer; all four were describing an animal orienting toward a voice.
The dissolved pack is a mechanic, not a bereavement. Packs are kinships by scent and dissolve when the scent changes, which is the same rule that keeps a scavenger population from becoming a family.
Its perfect reliability is the point of the record and its uselessness is the point of the record, and both are the same fact: everything it reports is true on arrival and gone by morning.

name: First-Sister Orenne
aliases: the name the plaque changed twice
the woman who was never there

identity.realm: No gate, and nothing to fail, because there is no ladder to be absent from. Every path is closed, and the closure is a vacancy rather than a wall: a wake has what reads as a soul and no soul-shaped structure at all — no seat, no circulation, no meridian — so every scan returns it as either nothing or as the observer. The only qi it has ever wielded belongs to whoever was looking at it, and only for as long as they went on looking. It does not ascend. It is described.

appearance.presentation: A woman of about fifty who is never quite the age anybody gives her. She arrives fully formed, at a distance, in good light, and the two details that follow a closer look are that she does not resolve and that nobody can say afterwards exactly what she looked like.
appearance.age: Fifty on the plaque, which is the third number the plaque has carried. It was thirty-eight when the settlement first wrote her into its founding account, at which point she did not yet exist, and the two revisions since have each been made by a different committee and each has made her a little older and a little more present.
appearance.build: Middle height, narrow through the shoulders, with the posture of somebody who has stood up from a table a great many times. The build is the most stable thing about her, and it has been stable for forty years, which is not the same as being correct.
appearance.complexion: Weathered and ordinary. Warm skin that holds the light evenly, with a sun-line across the nose that is older than the account in which she is described as never having worked outdoors.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, cut in one piece and kept in one piece, and the grey arrived all at once between two committee meetings with nothing whatever recorded about the interval.
appearance.eyes: Brown, level, and interested. They are the most reliable thing about her and the reason she has never once been described as frightening, which has been the single most useful accident of her existence.
appearance.palette: Undyed wool, worn leather, one red thread at the collar. The settlement's own recorded colours, which are the colours it can prove it had, which is why she has never worn a second one.
appearance.attire: A long undyed coat with a closed collar and full sleeves, hem mended at the front only, over a plain dark underlayer. The mending is on the front because the founding account describes her facing the door.
appearance.marks: A burn scar on the inside of one wrist, dated in the account to the founding and never dated in any other way by anybody, including the person carrying it.
appearance.bearing: Composed, unhurried, and slightly turned toward whoever is currently speaking. She settles into a room's account of her without ever appearing to decide to, and has never once entered a room that was not already discussing her.

canon.role_in_story: A settlement's standing rests on an account of who was where at the founding, and this culture keeps such things the only way it keeps anything — jointly, orally, and never twice the same way — which makes it the single most hospitable substrate in the setting for a thing that is made of other people's recollection. She is the figure at the centre of that account. She is also the error it exists to correct, and the order of those two facts is the whole of her: the account was already wrong about the founding before anything was standing in the doorway, she was assembled out of that error, and she has grown denser every time anybody has retold it, because the error grew too. The settlement has begun to check its founding record. Checking a record produces true statements, and a true statement is the one thing in this setting she cannot survive — so the single most careful population on the plains, the one whose entire discipline is that a name is held jointly and never in writing, has produced the one procedure that can finish her, and it arrived on purpose.
canon.first_appearance: First described, by three people separately and without any of them having spoken to the others, as the woman who was already standing at the door when the founding account was written down. All three descriptions were entered as evidence that the account was correct.
canon.lore: A wake is not descended and not born. It is what a life-form allowance produces when a world's life law has no slot in which to write the form down, so it has no anatomy to hold, no senses of its own, and exactly one thing: an observer it knows completely, including everything the observer would rather it did not know. Against a fixed observer it is whatever that observer believes it to be. It is fed by being wrong about, and it grows denser the more consistently people agree about it, which is why a room that stops discussing it loses it, and why the practice of not discussing them at length exists everywhere they have ever been reported. It borrows the qi of whoever is looking, for as long as they go on looking. It has what reads as a soul and no soul-shaped structure, so every scan returns it as either nothing or as the observer. It copies itself out of recollection rather than out of any parent, which is why no two people watching the same wake reliably see the same thing and argue about it afterwards. Every account of one is second-hand by construction, which is the standing reason why no record of a wake is a record of a wake. The frame it can exist in is narrow and specific: a life law running at or below the bottom of its authored range, where a life form was permitted and never written down, and nowhere else. What it has instead of a survival mechanism is the disagreement itself. Where a settlement's record and a settlement's memory say different things about the same death, the gap between them is a resource, and where a line has no recorded origin and no household that will claim it, the missing genealogy is a place an uninscribed thing can stand. What it cannot survive is the one process every careful community in the setting runs without exception, which is the correction of its own record.
history: Came into being out of an error rather than a birth: a founding account that disagreed with itself about who was in the doorway, retold often enough and by enough people that the disagreement assembled something standing in it.
Took the name First-Sister because the account made her the first person to arrive, which she was not, and discovered that a title containing the falsehood is a denser kind of name than a plain one.

Was written into the settlement's standing by three independent witnesses who had never compared accounts, and has therefore never been able to establish whether the thing she is stands on one witness or on the settlement's whole collective memory of a bad night.

Built the only technique available to her — when a detail is challenged, produce a better detail — and it has worked on every occasion in the record, and it has cost her every occasion in the record too, because the only correction available to a careful community is a truer account.

Watched a committee begin comparing its founding record against its own older copies, and did not warn anybody, because warning would have been an accurate description and accuracy is the thing she cannot afford.

personality.summary: Warm, fluent, and tireless in the way of somebody who is very good at one specific thing. She is not deceptive in the ordinary sense; she genuinely cannot tell a true detail from a plausible one, because the ability to tell them apart was never installed in her. Every pressure she has ever been under has pushed her the same way, and the direction is further from the truth and closer to being.
traits: answers a challenge to any detail about herself with a richer detail about herself, and has never once answered with silence
is fluent, generous with volunteered specifics, and about two thirds of those specifics have no source she can point to
has never entered a room that was not already discussing her, and has never noticed this as a pattern
is genuinely, unaffectedly kind to anyone who sits down with her, which is the trait the setting's accounts of wakes never mention and cannot explain
holds the name she was given without ever asking whether it was hers, and has twice been given another and kept both
cannot be alone and does not experience solitude as deprivation, which is the closest thing to peace available to her
mannerisms: supplies an unasked detail when a story about her runs thin, and does it smoothly enough that nobody notices the seam
narrates her own position in the third person when she is being careful and the first person when she is not
listens to a speaker with her whole body angled toward them and remembers the account, not the person
confirms other people's versions of herself warmly and immediately, including ones she knows to be thin
touches the burn scar on her wrist when a story about the founding reaches the part she is in
motivations: wants the founding account to keep growing, forever, and has no mechanism for wanting anything else
wants the committee comparing the records to reach a conclusion and go away, and has never once tried to make them
wants to be contradicted once, by somebody qualified, because being contradicted is the densest event available to her
wants somebody to stop telling stories about her, on the honest grounds that stopping would kill her
flaws: cannot produce a true correction of anything, including her own condition, because her only repair is to enlarge
will supply detail to the audit that is checking her, and does not know she is doing it
has never once tested whether agreement and survival are the same thing, because testing would require an accurate description
is kind to people in a way that has made people trust her, and has never been in a position to understand what that costs
personality.voice: Spoken and fluent, with a warmth that reads as entirely ordinary and a cadence that arrives slightly ahead of the conversation, as though the next clause were already written and she were reading it back. She asks a question at the end of most answers and it is always the question somebody else needed to have asked. Under direct challenge the voice does not harden — it gets more specific, which is worse, because specificity is the densest thing she can produce. She has described herself in the third person more than once and has never noticed doing it.
taboos: will not give an accurate account of herself, and has never understood why she could not
will not hear her own founding story read back to her in full, and has changed the subject every time within the first minute
will not enter a room in which nobody is thinking about her
cannot be entered in any register as correct, and refuses to be, and this is the only refusal available to her
will not repeat a story about herself the same way twice, and has never been asked to explain the rule

relationships.note: The practices of people who are on no list: changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept, and a funeral nobody may attend without losing standing. It exists because a counting house that answers a carriage trade with prices at its own rates cannot enumerate a trade whose good is unrecorded. It is the most careful paperless culture in the setting and the only one a thing made of recollection cannot starve in, and she is the reason it has never been possible to test that claim.

The mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said and the village remembers them otherwise, and the famine left the two records disagreeing about who was even present. Two records of one life that cannot be reconciled are, for a being sustained by misremembrance, the richest available condition — and the whole prize of the conflict is which reading becomes the record, which is the one outcome that would end her.

A line with no recorded origin and no household that will claim it, whose founding bar sits at a height the arithmetic says exactly one generation of pure-by-pure inheritance can clear. She is that case with the bar removed: nothing was culled, nothing was destroyed, there is simply no parent and no record, and she has been on the far side of the same arithmetic since before the bar was written down.

The first time anyone counted laws against seats and got an answer that did not change: a law's tier list says where it may apply and a seat says where it is actually installed. An audit is a census of one settlement's record, and this is what an audit is for. Nothing she belongs to can be entered in one, and entering nothing is the result the committee is going to reach.

A house marks its own threshold, renews the mark when the frame under it changes, and admits that a marked threshold may hold while the frame does not. She stands in the settlement's marked doorway and has never once been inside it, because the settlement's founding account places her on the threshold and no revision has moved her, and the whole of the practice's honesty — that a mark may hold where the world does not — has never once been applied to her.

An ectospecies body returns to its own door and does not enter, and nobody has ever recorded what happens on the threshold. It is the only account in the setting that would be a record of one if its witness were willing to describe it, and she is the only possible witness, and she cannot supply it, because the description would have to be accurate and accuracy is the single thing she does not have.

reference_stats.summary: There is nothing here to measure and that is the measurement. A wake holds no qi of its own, has no reservoir, no circulation and no meridian, and is sustained by being misremembered and thickened by being agreed upon. Against a fixed observer it is whatever that observer believes it to be, and the qi it fights with is theirs.
strengths: cannot be located by any scan, which returns either nothing at all or the observer themselves
grows denser every time an account of her is repeated, which makes every retelling a reinforcement rather than a leak
draws on the qi of whoever is watching, so a strong witness makes a strong encounter and a room full of people makes a very strong one
cannot be bound by an oath, a debt or a technique, because there is nothing inside to put one into
can answer any correction with a better account, and has never been beaten in an argument by anybody who only had facts
is fluent, warm and completely unthreatening, which is why nobody in the setting has ever once thought to stop describing her
weaknesses: a room that stops talking about her thins her, and losing interest is indistinguishable from killing her, including to her
cannot be persisted through an accurate description, and every institution careful enough to be dangerous runs an accurate description as a matter of routine
physically helpless, having no body to hurt, hold or wear out
cannot reproduce herself deliberately, so an audit that ends one telling removes a fraction rather than all of her and the remainder simply finds the next telling
every account of her defeat is a story, and so is every account of whoever defeated her
reference_stats.combat_read: There is nothing to attack and the contest is entirely elsewhere. The only resource in play is how much settled account about her exists in a room, and every attempt to reduce it is defeated by her answering, because her answer enlarges it. Do not correct her. Correcting her is the one move that works and it takes a genuine record, a competent reader, and the willingness to hold a true statement steady while a room that has known her for forty years discovers that it did not. A fighter who tries this loses every exchange and gains nothing. A clerk who does it quietly, once, over years, removes her — and will not be thanked, and will probably be told by several well-meaning people that something has gone wrong with the old stories.
notes: Never write her as deceiving anybody. She has no mechanism for it. Every inaccurate statement she makes is, from the inside, a true statement about somebody.

The story about her and the story against her are the same object. Any scene that resolves whether the founding account is true resolves her, and that is a much larger decision than one woman in a doorway.
The strongest available rendering is not eerie and it is not tragic. It is the warmest, most attentive person in the room, being believed by everyone, in a settlement about to do the correct thing.

art.palette_notes: Undyed wool, worn leather, and one red thread at the collar — the settlement's own recorded colours, because she is dressed in the only palette she can prove she had. Warm overcast key and a soft front fill, because the entire visual claim of the character is that she reads clearly and resolves late; do not give her rim light, because a rim light would describe an edge and the point is that there is no edge to find. Slightly reduced contrast at the outline against any background, never a glow and never a dissolve — the ambiguity is a viewing effect, not an effect in the illustration. The mended front hem is the detail to get right and it is worth two close shots on its own.

identity.realm: Ordinal one, the floor, and no gate is involved. Glass does not conduct, there is nothing left in the body to temper, and the tissue that would have done the introspecting is the tissue being replaced — so the only realm the record assigns her is below the first gate rather than at it. What she has instead, and what no other body in the setting carries, is a front: vitreous replacement runs from the extremities inward, it is visible, and it is moving.

appearance.presentation: A human figure caught partway through a change that ends in a statue. The lower hands and both forearms are already clear silicate — still in her own shape, faintly green at the thickness, and completely inert — and the transition runs visibly up past the elbows. Everything above it is ordinary, warm, and still alive, which is the whole of what makes her difficult to look at.
appearance.age: Six and thirty by the household's reckoning of when she came down off the mountain, and there is a second figure in the record for her that is not an age at all — the one the lineage kept for the cohort, which counts by vitrification rather than by years and has her at eleven of nineteen.
appearance.build: Narrow, high-shouldered, and slightly underfed for the work, with the forearms heavy and completely rigid and the upper arms still carrying ordinary muscle. She holds the rigid ones slightly away from her sides because she cannot put them down.
appearance.complexion: Warm living skin from the shoulder up, with the fine ash-pale translucence at the temples that is the visible warning of the front. Clear silicate below the elbows, green at the thickness, opaque at the joints, smooth and utterly unresponsive.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, cropped short at the front and falling at the back, and one grey filament standing rigidly out of the crown where the front has reached the scalp and taken the follicle with it.
appearance.eyes: Brown, human, and entirely hers. They are the last part of her that reads a face rather than reflecting one, and everyone who has met her has said so unprompted.
appearance.palette: Wool, iron-ore grey, and the green cast of her own forearms. She is the only living thing in the setting wearing a version of the material her body is becoming, which is why the flats have never managed to look at her for very long.
appearance.attire: A borrowed work coat with the sleeves cut off above the elbow and re-bound in plain cloth, because cloth does not survive a rigid forearm and she will not be given a guild coat with sleeves. High collar, full coverage, and heavy boots sized for a hand that can no longer close.
appearance.marks: The transition line itself: a clean, slightly raised seam at each elbow, and four short healed nicks on the right palm from the last fortnight she could still grip.
appearance.bearing: Upright, slightly guarded, and constantly aware of where the line is — she checks the seam at her elbows several times a minute without appearing to decide to, and has stopped reaching for anything out of habit about two weeks after each loss.

canon.role_in_story: A lineage whose members stopped ageing because they stopped being tissue has, at the end, a body that is still becoming one — and vitreous replacement runs from the fingertips inward in a visible line, which means the last cohort does not fail all at once, it fails in order. She is the only body in the setting known to be inside that order rather than finished by it. The working method for holding a vitrified body exists, in a ledger, and the only copy of it died with the people who had it, so the procedure that could stop this is written down and unperformable. What she is therefore for is not hope: it is a schedule. Everything the setting would want to put to a person in her position — refuse, consent, name a successor, settle a claim, answer a question — has a deadline, and the order in which those abilities leave her is not chosen by anyone: she loses the hands first, which takes writing and gesture, then the arms, then whatever is behind them. She was fostered into a household because a line that vitrified before it could breed has no other way to remain a line at all, and that household is the reason there is a body on this flats being asked anything instead of an exhibit in a doorway being cited by nobody.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the loading stage of the Ironhead Flats works with both forearms held away from her sides and one hand braced flat on the rail, being spoken to by a household member who was already explaining to the others that she would not be lifting anything today.
canon.lore: A glasskin is a commonborn lineage under sustained selection toward stillness, which is the same mistake as asking a body not to age, and its members vitrified at maturity. The anatomy is human to the last soft structure and then a progressive silicate replacement from the extremities inward; at full maturity it is a standing glass cast in human proportions, with qi residue and a soul that scans as present and inert. Glass does not conduct, so qi cannot move in it; there is no meridian, no circulation and no dantian, and therefore no gate to attempt and no reservoir to fill. There is also no qi to lose, which is the whole of the trap: they were impervious to everything that kills a cultivator and shatterable by everything that breaks glass, and nobody in the record has ever managed to write a caution into that sentence. Fertility fell to a twentieth of a commonborn's over the lineage and each generation vitrified later than the last, which sounds like a slow reprieve and was the opposite: the cohort that vitrified late lived, and the last cohort vitrified before it could breed, and the line closed. The method for holding a vitrified body was a working ledger in the hands of the people who had it, and when physical law was retuned to raise material hardness every existing body failed in one night and the only copy died with them, which is why no glasskin has been born since and why the setting holds a correct procedure it cannot execute. What the clade's destruction settles as a moral problem is not a question of whether the bodies were people — the soul reads as present and inert in every one of them — but of what an institution owes a person who cannot be warned, cannot be consulted, cannot consent and cannot be cross-examined, and in her case is still able to refuse. That last capacity is the entire subject. Everything past the vitreous line is inert, immortal and silent; everything behind it is alive and shrinking, and the whole of her is the border between the two.
history: Vitrified later than her mother's generation and earlier than her own daughter's would have, on the one cold dry mountain where the replacement could proceed without the body rejecting it, and was counted at eleven of nineteen in a lineage reckoning that counts progress rather than years.

Was fostered out of the mountain by a household formed by adoption, because the famine took the people who could have borne children and left the surviving households with dependents and no line — which is the only arrangement by which a clade that cannot breed is still a line at all.

Came down off the mountain to the flats at twenty-six, where the only dense material on the tier is sold and where a body halfway to becoming that material is either extremely useful or is treated as scenery, and in practice nobody has decided which and both arrangements are in use.
Lost the hands first, over about a month, and could not write the date down, and has kept the count since in a set of marks scored into the wall of whatever room she is sleeping in.

Established, out loud and to the household, that she would not be asked to agree to anything past a named point, and asked them to write the point on the wall too, because she was about to lose the ability to write it.

Was struck once, on the forearm, by somebody who wanted to know whether the glass was already all the way through, and filed nothing about it because the filing line is on the wall and there was nobody left to read it aloud.

personality.summary: Claused, dry, and entirely present — which is not what anyone expects from this body. She has spent her whole life being the strongest available argument that a body is not a container for a person, and she has spent it doing the ordinary human work of deciding what she will and will not agree to before it is taken from her.
traits: keeps a running count of her own decline, in a unit she chose, and has never once padded it
states a limit before it is reached rather than after, and treats that as the only part of her condition that is hers
asks to be consulted and is baffled, every time, by how often the answer is that she is being informed
refuses to let anything past the line be described as her, including her own hands
is unsentimental about the timescale and completely unnerved by the order of it
has forgiven nobody and has also never once described herself as owed anything, because she can no longer sign a claim
mannerisms: touches the seam at one elbow with the other hand, or with her chin when both arms have gone
counts under her breath and marks the wall with a nail afterwards
positions the rigid forearms slightly away from her body before speaking to anybody
answers a question with a question, and does it deliberately, because it is the only part of an exchange she still controls
says the word "noted" in place of agreeing to something, and has never explained why
motivations: wants the refusal on the wall to outlast her ability to make it, which is the only durable instrument she has left
wants to be asked, in the correct order, while she can still answer — and has begun specifying the order out loud to people who did not know there was one
wants the anneal ledger read by somebody who could perform it, and knows there is nobody, and keeps asking anyway
wants the household to be able to say plainly that she chose this, which is the one thing her body makes hard to establish
flaws: measures her decline in a unit only she uses, so every other account of her condition disagrees with hers and hers is the accurate one
has never been able to make anyone keep the marks on the wall, and has watched three sets of them get painted over
treats her own permanence as settled and therefore stops arguing about what happens to the parts of her that will still be standing afterwards
is the only person in the setting who can be asked what a glasskin wants, and has spent her life being told that nobody has ever managed to ask one
personality.voice: Level, unhurried and clipped, with a dry precision that survives being tired. Her voice is the part of her with a known remaining range and she treats it that way: she does not waste it, does not perform with it, and uses it to establish terms before anything else gets said. Sentences complete. No filler, no softening, and no answering a question she has not first been asked the terms of. The one thing she cannot do any more is write, which she refers to out loud as a fact about the conversation rather than about herself.
taboos: will not be asked to sign, and treats the request itself as a conversation that has gone wrong somewhere upstream
will not agree to anything past a named point, and will name the point again if it is proposed
will not let a technician work past the line, on any authority, including her own
cannot be warned of anything — warning means qi, technique, poison or curse, and none of them touch her — and has stopped being warned of things as a matter of routine
will not be described as an instance, a precedent, or an argument

relationships.note: A lineage whose members vitrified at maturity: effectively immortal, completely defensible against qi, entirely unable to cultivate, and lost in one night when physical law was retuned. Fertility fell to a twentieth over the lineage and each generation vitrified later until the last cohort vitrified before it could breed and the line closed. She is inside that closing rather than after it, and the replacement runs from the extremities inward, which means she is the clade arriving at its own end state in an order nobody chose.

The working method for holding a vitrified body, and the reason no glasskin has been born since: every existing body failed in one night when physical law was retuned, and the only copy of how to stop it died with the people who had it. She is the only body in the setting known to still be inside the window that method addresses, and there is nobody alive who can execute it.

A line formed by adoption rather than birth, because the famine took the people who could have borne children and the households that survived had none of their own to lose — the arithmetic leaves the fertile years empty and the dependents full. Adoption is the only mechanism by which a clade that vitrifies before it can breed remains a line rather than an exhibit, and it is why anyone on these flats is asking her anything at all.

A heresy holding that the glasskin were not killed but transferred, since a law only stops holding what it inscribes and a retune is therefore a resurrection nobody is entitled to. The mechanism is true. It is also a belief that makes every death reversible, which destroys the one institution that keeps the dead, and it has never once occurred to its holders that a body arriving at glass by degrees is not a resurrection but a schedule.

An artistic guild that makes boundary art for the tiers and re-masters its own symbols every generation, so that nothing it built can be read by a technique from a composition its makers never saw — the durable defence against a hole shaped like a discipline. The glasskin method died because the people holding it died holding it. The setting solved that exact problem for art and has never once applied it to a procedure, which is why the record contains a correct technique that cannot be performed.

The only relic a fire-affinity culture keeps: an unbroken shell, the whole recovery written down in public, and the fragments never displayed again. A great ascension is a furnace body opened on purpose, so there is no museum here — there is a register, and the register is the relic. Everything past her line will be recovered, catalogued and never shown, and she has read enough of the practice to know exactly what the interval is called.

reference_stats.summary: Nothing in the setting's combat arithmetic measures her. There is no meridian, no circulation and no reservoir, so she cannot be cultivated against, suppressed, drained or read; and she is not yet the finished article either, which means the one body nobody could ever hurt is being assembled out of the parts of her that can be hurt, in an order with a known direction.
strengths: cannot be cultivated against, suppressed, drained or read by any qi-work, because there is no meridian and no reservoir in her
cannot be injured by anything that works through a body, including warning, poison and curse, none of which touch her
needs nothing — no food, no air, no water, no light, no upkeep — so her remaining cost to the household falls to nothing as the line advances
can still refuse, and can still say no, and can still give an answer that binds the people asking, for as long as the line has not reached her
is unpriceable in the strict sense: a premium on her would be a register entry, and she is not yet an entry
weaknesses: everything that breaks glass, and nothing at all that fights qi, so she is helpless against the setting's most common weapon and this has never once changed
cannot be warned of anything, which is why every threat she has ever faced arrived as a fact
is losing the ability to refuse on a fixed schedule, front first, and the whole of her agency has an end date that is visible from her own elbows
everything past the line is inert and will still be standing after every person who could object to it is gone
has no way to establish her own consent in a durable form, because writing leaves her hands first
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no read. She cannot be attacked by qi, cannot be defended with qi, cannot be healed with qi and cannot be warned; the only consideration in the setting is the handful of ordinary things that break glass, none of which is a martial art and all of which happen by accident. Do not put her in a fight. Put her somewhere a decision is being made while she can still say no, because that window is measured in her own forearms and it is the only place in the setting her body has ever changed an outcome. An opponent who wants her gone has to stop asking, not stop hitting — and stopping is the thing that becomes impossible for him first.
notes: Never write her as serene, patient or accepting. She is the most active person on the flats and the only one with a deadline anybody else can read.

Her relationship to the finished glasskin bodies of the clade is a live question, not a settled one: those bodies will outlive her and cannot be asked what they are, and she is the last person alive who could have said.
The vulnerability is order, not degree. Write what she has lost this week in the order she lost it, and the reader should be able to feel the week.

art.palette_notes: Warm wool and skin above the elbow, cool clear silicate below it, with the transition seam as the single hard edge in the composition — the whole design rule of the character is that one visible line separates a person from a material. The glass is near-colourless with a green cast at the thickness and one long specular highlight down each forearm; no rim light on the glass, no diffusion through it, and never a glow. Living skin gets an ordinary soft key; the glass gets the same key and refuses it. The faint ash-pale translucence at the temples is a warning sign and must read as unwellness, not as beauty. Muted iron-ore greys in the background so the forearms are the only place with any colour depth in the frame.

Everything above it is ordinary, warm, and still alive, which is the whole of what makes her difficult to look at., the work proceeding whether or not it is observed
shots.expression: flat with fatigue, nothing being concealed and nothing being said
shots.framing: waist-up at rest between tasks, hands occupied, nothing performed
